newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX crude ends higher on IPL pipeline troubles.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX crude ends higher on IPL pipeline troubles.

text.p: NYMEX crude prices ended higher Monday after Interprovincial Pipe Line (IPL) said that a power outage in Minnesota hit three of its pumping stations and took out a million barrels per day (bpd) of throughput from its pipeline.
Monday's positive settlement in crude was the first in five sessions, with May crude ending 11 cents up at $19.23 a barrel. Still, spot crude ended 39 cents off its session high.
"It's a lot of volume to be shut (but) there has been a pattern since last week of late session sell-offs," said Tim Evans, analyst with Pegasus Econometric Group in New York.
May gasoline ended up 0.24 cent at 60.72 cents a gallon while May heating oil finished off 0.02 cent a gallon at 53.12 cents.
The IPL system had been carrying about 1.4 million bpd and comprises several pipelines which run from western Canada through the U.S. Midwest to Quebec and upstate New York.

The lines that are shut carry light, medium, heavy and synthetic crudes plus condesate. The power outage was caused by a severe snowstorm in the Northern Plains of the United States. IPL said that it would not be until Wednesday at the earliest when the pumping stations could resume operations.
Last week, May crude lost almost $1.75 a barrel as views of ample supply driven by increasing imports have engulfed the market in a bearish trend.

Reflecting the surfeit, May crude's contango to June ended at 10 cents, steady with Friday's level, despite Monday's announcement of supply disruption. Contango indicates the contract nearer time is cheaper than the later contract.
Traders were skeptical that Monday's gains in crude would place oil prices on the road to upward recovery.
"We would have to settle strong, meaning at least near the session highs, for that to happen," said Ed Kevelson, director of refined products with Paribas Futures Inc in New York.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
